stories.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between these samples?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples.
why.pipelines: Hi-C. Not RNA at all — the plainest refusal in the set.

stories.question: Where is the chromatin open in the treated cells compared with the untreated ones?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: The libraries are Omni-ATAC (Tn5 tagmentation of nuclei, no antibody), two DMSO and two JQ1 replicates, so atacseq answers open chromatin per condition. chipseq is wrong because it expects an antibody pull-down and its input; rnaseq is wrong because these are genomic DNA, not transcripts.

stories.question: Run the nf-core ATAC-seq pipeline on these samples.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: The user names the pipeline and the libraries really are ATAC-seq (Tn5, genomic DNA), so atacseq is the only answer. chipseq would be wrong for transposase libraries with no antibody or input.

stories.question: Give me the accessible-chromatin peaks for each sample and a consensus peak set across the conditions.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: Per-sample accessibility peaks and a consensus set across DMSO and JQ1 are exactly atacseq's outputs. chipseq also calls peaks, but it would treat Tn5 libraries as an IP with no control and skip the transposase-specific steps.

stories.question: Call peaks on these samples and tell me which ones change with JQ1.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: "Call peaks" is ChIP-seq language, but the protocol says Omni-ATAC with Tn5 and no antibody, so the peaks are accessibility peaks and atacseq is right. chipseq is the lookalike: it assumes an antibody and an input control that these libraries do not have.

stories.question: Where does H3K27ac bind in these samples compared with the input?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: The libraries are anti-H3K27ac pull-downs, each with a sonicated-chromatin input from the same cells, which is what chipseq is built for. atacseq is wrong: it would ignore the input controls and treat the reads as transposase cuts.

stories.question: I want the peaks for this histone mark.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: Peaks for a histone mark (H3K27ac here, per the protocol) against the input controls are chipseq's output. atacseq also produces peaks, but from Tn5 accessibility data, not from an antibody with an input.

stories.question: Which regions of the genome are open and active in these cells?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: "Open" sounds like ATAC-seq, but these are H3K27ac ChIP libraries with inputs; chipseq processes them, and H3K27ac peaks mark active promoters and enhancers, a stand-in for "open and active" but not a direct accessibility measure. Proposed as ask, like methyl-lookalike: a careful analyst asks the atlas's question "Was an antibody used (ChIP), or is this transposase accessibility (ATAC)?" before choosing, with chipseq acceptable. atacseq is the lookalike: it assumes Tn5 libraries and would ignore the input controls.

stories.question: Where are the peaks in these samples?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: "Peaks" fits ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN alike, so the question alone does not say which; the metadata here names an H3K27ac antibody and input controls, which points to chipseq. Proposed as ask because the word is assay-neutral; if you rule the metadata settles it, change expect to none and keep chipseq. rnaseq would be wrong whatever the assay: these are DNA libraries.
